symptom: `docker pull` from private registry fails 'unauthorized: incorrect username or password' OR 'denied: requested access to the resource is denied' OR 'pull access denied for X, repository does not exist or may require docker login'
error_patterns: repository does not exist or may require docker login

diagnostic_steps.action: Identify what wording the error uses (narrows the cause)
diagnostic_steps.command: docker pull <image> 2>&1 | tail -3
diagnostic_steps.expected: 'pull access denied' = no/bad creds; 'toomanyrequests' = rate limit (different fm); 'denied' alone = repo policy

diagnostic_steps.action: Check what credentials docker has
diagnostic_steps.command: cat ~/.docker/config.json 2>/dev/null | jq '.auths | keys'
diagnostic_steps.expected: list of registry hostnames you've logged into; if missing your registry, no creds at all

diagnostic_steps.action: Test auth directly against the registry's v2 API
diagnostic_steps.command: curl -u "$USER:$PASS" -I https://<registry>/v2/<org>/<repo>/manifests/latest
diagnostic_steps.expected: 200=auth+repo OK; 401=auth bad; 404=auth OK but repo/tag wrong

diagnostic_steps.action: For ECR specifically, check token age (12-hour expiry)
diagnostic_steps.command: aws sts get-caller-identity && aws ecr get-login-password --region <region> | head -c 20
diagnostic_steps.expected: sts works → IAM ok; if get-login-password fails, IAM perms issue not token age

fix_steps.action: For Docker Hub / GHCR / Harbor: re-login
fix_steps.command: docker login <registry>
fix_steps.validation: docker pull succeeds

fix_steps.action: For ECR: refresh the 12-hour token now AND wire into CI to refresh per-job
fix_steps.command: aws ecr get-login-password --region us-east-1 | docker login --username AWS --password-stdin <account>.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com
fix_steps.validation: ~/.docker/config.json has fresh auth entry

fix_steps.action: For GitHub Actions / shared CI: use the official login action so it refreshes per-job
fix_steps.command: # .github/workflows/x.yml: - uses: aws-actions/amazon-ecr-login@v2  # or docker/login-action@v3
fix_steps.validation: subsequent steps inherit auth; no stale token

fix_steps.action: For cluster pulls (EKS/ECS): switch from imagePullSecrets to IRSA / task IAM role so pulls use the assumed role's automatically-refreshed token
fix_steps.command: # EKS: annotate ServiceAccount with eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn=<arn> that has AmazonEC2ContainerRegistryReadOnly
fix_steps.validation: kubelet can pull without imagePullSecret

symptom: systemd unit goes 'failed' after StartLimitBurst (5 by default) restarts; further `systemctl start` returns 'start-limit-hit' until counter is reset

diagnostic_steps.action: Get the current state + last 10 journal lines
diagnostic_steps.command: sudo systemctl status <unit> --no-pager -l
diagnostic_steps.expected: Active: failed (Result: start-limit-hit); recent restart count

diagnostic_steps.action: Read the FULL unit log for the actual underlying error
diagnostic_steps.command: sudo journalctl -u <unit> -e --no-pager
diagnostic_steps.expected: the binary's real exit reason (status=2/INVALIDARGUMENT, status=203/EXEC, YAML parse error, etc.) BEFORE the start-limit-hit message

diagnostic_steps.action: Verify the unit file isn't malformed
diagnostic_steps.command: sudo systemd-analyze verify <unit>
diagnostic_steps.expected: silent = OK; any output = unit-file syntax issue

diagnostic_steps.action: Inspect StartLimit settings
diagnostic_steps.command: systemctl show <unit> -p StartLimitBurst,StartLimitIntervalSec,Restart,RestartSec
diagnostic_steps.expected: defaults: Burst=5, Interval=10s, Restart=on-failure (or 'no' = never restarts)

fix_steps.action: Fix the underlying error first (see step 2 of diagnostic). DON'T just reset the counter — it'll just hit the limit again
fix_steps.command: # edit config / fix permissions / fix ExecStart path, then:
fix_steps.validation: running the binary directly succeeds: sudo -u <user> /path/to/bin --check-config

fix_steps.action: Reset the failure counter, then start
fix_steps.command: sudo systemctl reset-failed <unit> && sudo systemctl start <unit> && sudo systemctl status <unit>
fix_steps.validation: Active: active (running); journal shows clean startup

fix_steps.action: Loosen StartLimit so transient failures don't lock you out
fix_steps.command:
# edit /etc/systemd/system/<unit>.d/restart.conf:
# [Unit]
# StartLimitIntervalSec=600s
# StartLimitBurst=10
# [Service]
# Restart=on-failure
# RestartSec=5s
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
fix_steps.validation: systemctl show shows new values; transient failure no longer locks unit

fix_steps.action: Add ExecStartPre to validate config before main process starts (catches bad config early without consuming a restart slot)
fix_steps.command: # [Service]\n# ExecStartPre=/usr/local/bin/<bin> --config-check /etc/<bin>.yaml\n# ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/<bin> --config /etc/<bin>.yaml
fix_steps.validation: bad config now fails ExecStartPre with clear error, never starts main process

symptom: DNS lookups inside pods take 3-5 seconds for external hostnames (api.stripe.com, s3.amazonaws.com) — search-domain amplification with the default ndots:5

diagnostic_steps.action: Show pod's resolv.conf — confirm ndots and search list
diagnostic_steps.command: kubectl exec <pod> -- cat /etc/resolv.conf
diagnostic_steps.expected: options ndots:5 + search <ns>.svc.cluster.local svc.cluster.local cluster.local — that's the source

diagnostic_steps.action: Time a no-trailing-dot lookup (triggers search expansion)
diagnostic_steps.command: kubectl exec <pod> -- sh -c 'time getent hosts api.stripe.com 2>&1'
diagnostic_steps.expected: ~3 seconds total (4 NXDOMAINs at ~750ms each, then the real lookup)

diagnostic_steps.action: Time a trailing-dot lookup (FQDN, skips search) for comparison
diagnostic_steps.command: kubectl exec <pod> -- sh -c 'time getent hosts api.stripe.com. 2>&1'
diagnostic_steps.expected: <100ms — confirms search expansion is the issue

diagnostic_steps.action: Cross-check CoreDNS isn't also slow on its end
diagnostic_steps.command: kubectl exec <pod> -- dig +tries=1 +time=2 @$(kubectl get svc -n kube-system kube-dns -o jsonpath='{.spec.clusterIP}') api.stripe.com.
diagnostic_steps.expected: <100ms; if slow here too, the issue is in CoreDNS or upstream, not search

fix_steps.action: Pod-side fix: set ndots:2 via dnsConfig.options (no app change)
fix_steps.command:
# spec.dnsPolicy: ClusterFirst
# spec.dnsConfig:
#   options:
#     - name: ndots
#       value: "2"
kubectl rollout restart deploy/<name>
fix_steps.validation: new pod's resolv.conf shows ndots:2; getent hosts api.stripe.com finishes <100ms
fix_steps.rollback: remove dnsConfig from spec; rollout restart

fix_steps.action: App-code fix: append trailing dot for known external services
fix_steps.command: # Python: requests.get('https://api.stripe.com.')\n# Go: http.Get('https://api.stripe.com./...')\n# In env: APP_API_URL=https://api.stripe.com.
fix_steps.validation: app's outbound calls measurably faster; CoreDNS metric coredns_dns_responses_total{rcode="NXDOMAIN"} drops

fix_steps.action: Cluster-wide fix: configure CoreDNS to short-circuit known external suffixes (advanced; only if many teams hit this)
fix_steps.validation: reduced search-amplification load on CoreDNS

symptom: Devin DevBox can't reach internal/private service (staging.internal.acme.io). Session log: 'Could not resolve host', or 'connection timed out', or 'self-signed certificate in certificate chain'

diagnostic_steps.action: Classify the error (DNS vs TCP vs TLS — different fixes)
diagnostic_steps.command:
# session log shows one of:
# 'Could not resolve host' → DNS
# 'Connection timed out' / 'No route' → routing/firewall
# 'self-signed certificate' → TLS trust
diagnostic_steps.expected: narrows to one of three branches

diagnostic_steps.action: From inside DevBox terminal: test the layers
diagnostic_steps.command: # DNS:  getent hosts staging.internal.acme.io\n# Routing: curl -v --max-time 5 https://10.50.1.5/health  (use IP not name)\n# TLS:  openssl s_client -connect staging.internal.acme.io:443 -servername staging.internal.acme.io < /dev/null 2>&1 | head -20
diagnostic_steps.expected: identifies which layer fails

diagnostic_steps.action: Check VPN client state
diagnostic_steps.command: pgrep -a openvpn; ip addr show tun0 2>/dev/null | head -3; tail -20 /var/log/openvpn/*.log 2>/dev/null
diagnostic_steps.expected: openvpn daemon running + tun0 has IP + log shows 'Initialization Sequence Completed'

diagnostic_steps.action: Check VPN-pushed DNS landed in resolv.conf
diagnostic_steps.command: cat /etc/resolv.conf
diagnostic_steps.expected: nameserver line pointing at internal DNS (10.x or similar); search line for internal domain

fix_steps.action: For VPN not running: ensure blueprint setup actually starts it (config alone isn't enough)
fix_steps.command: # environment.yaml setup: |\n#   sudo openvpn --config /etc/openvpn/client.conf --auth-user-pass /etc/openvpn/auth.txt --daemon --writepid /run/openvpn.pid\n#   for i in $(seq 1 30); do ip link show tun0 >/dev/null 2>&1 && break; sleep 1; done
fix_steps.validation: new session: ip addr show tun0 succeeds within 30s of boot

fix_steps.action: For DNS-only failure: inject internal DNS via blueprint
fix_steps.command:
# environment.yaml setup: |
#   echo 'nameserver 10.50.1.1' | sudo tee /etc/resolv.conf
#   echo 'nameserver 8.8.8.8' | sudo tee -a /etc/resolv.conf  # public fallback
#   echo 'search internal.acme.io' | sudo tee -a /etc/resolv.conf
fix_steps.validation: getent hosts staging.internal.acme.io returns internal IP

fix_steps.action: For TLS untrusted: install corp CA bundle into DevBox trust store
fix_steps.command: # environment.yaml: secrets: [{name: CORP_CA, target: /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/corp.crt}]\n# setup: sudo update-ca-certificates
fix_steps.validation: openssl s_client shows verify return code: 0 (ok); curl https://internal works

fix_steps.action: For language runtimes (Java/Node/Python) with their own trust stores
fix_steps.command: # Java: keytool -import -trustcacerts -keystore $JAVA_HOME/lib/security/cacerts -file corp.crt -alias corp\n# Node: export NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/usr/local/share/ca-certificates/corp.crt\n# Python: export REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE=/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt
fix_steps.validation: per-runtime test (java client, node app, python script) succeeds against internal HTTPS

symptom: App is slow under load but `top`/`kubectl top` shows low CPU usage (e.g. 35%) and no errors. RED metrics look fine; only latency is degraded. Classic Brendan Gregg 'CPU utilization is wrong' scenario.

diagnostic_steps.action: Check IPC (instructions per cycle) — distinguishes 'CPU stalled' from 'CPU truly idle'
diagnostic_steps.command: sudo perf stat -p $(pgrep -f <app>) -- sleep 10
diagnostic_steps.expected: healthy: IPC > 1.0; suspicious: IPC < 0.5; severely stalled: IPC < 0.2 — means CPU is 'busy' but waiting on memory/cache/branch-mispredict

diagnostic_steps.action: Off-CPU analysis — where is the thread blocked?
diagnostic_steps.command: sudo offcputime-bpfcc -p $(pgrep -f <app>) 30 2>&1 | tail -30  # OR  sudo perf record -F 99 -e sched:sched_switch -g --call-graph dwarf -p <pid> -- sleep 30
diagnostic_steps.expected: top off-CPU stacks point at lock (futex_wait), IO (io_schedule), socket (tcp_recvmsg), or DB driver

diagnostic_steps.action: Check cgroup CFS throttling (containerized workloads)
diagnostic_steps.command: cat /sys/fs/cgroup/<cg>/cpu.stat   # OR for k8s pod: kubectl exec <pod> -- cat /sys/fs/cgroup/cpu.stat
diagnostic_steps.expected: nr_throttled non-zero AND increasing = CPU limit being hit even though average looks fine

diagnostic_steps.action: Check Pressure Stall Information (PSI) for memory + CPU + IO contention
diagnostic_steps.command: cat /proc/pressure/cpu /proc/pressure/io /proc/pressure/memory
diagnostic_steps.expected: avg10/avg60/avg300 percentages; non-trivial 'some' or 'full' = saturation we'd otherwise miss

fix_steps.action: For low-IPC + futex_wait combo: lock contention. Find the lock + shrink critical section
fix_steps.command: # Generate flame graph: perf record -g --call-graph dwarf -p <pid> -- sleep 30; perf script | flamegraph.pl > offcpu.svg\n# Identify the lock; refactor app: move expensive work outside critical section, switch to RWMutex if many readers, or shard state
fix_steps.validation: IPC rises above 1.0; off-CPU futex stacks shrink; p99 latency drops

fix_steps.action: For cgroup throttling: widen quota window (longer period accommodates bursts)
fix_steps.command: # k8s: spec.containers[].resources.limits.cpu: '4'  # raise limit\n# OR: kubeletConfig CPUManagerPolicy=static if predictable cores available
fix_steps.validation: cpu.stat nr_throttled stops increasing under same load

fix_steps.action: For low IPC w/ no off-CPU: memory bandwidth or NUMA. Pin app to one node + check LLC misses
fix_steps.command: sudo perf stat -e cycles,instructions,LLC-loads,LLC-load-misses -p <pid> -- sleep 10\n# If LLC miss rate >10%: numactl --cpunodebind=0 --membind=0 ./<app>
fix_steps.validation: LLC miss rate drops; IPC rises

symptom: Postmortem turns into blame; engineer at risk of leaving; adjacent teams now avoiding deploy assignments; reporting culture chilling effect

diagnostic_steps.action: Review the postmortem doc for blame language
diagnostic_steps.command: # Search for: engineer's name appearing as subject of failure verbs ('Sarah forgot', 'X didn't notice')\n# Versus role-based, system-level framing ('the deploy process didn't catch')
diagnostic_steps.expected: if names appear as subjects of failures, framing is broken

diagnostic_steps.action: Check the action items — are they 'be more careful' or system-level?
diagnostic_steps.command: # 'Sarah will be more careful' → failed framing\n# 'Add YAML schema validation in CI' / 'Add 60s canary period' → system-level (correct)
diagnostic_steps.expected: action items target the system, not the human

diagnostic_steps.action: Survey the chilling effect: any engineers avoiding deploys / on-call?
diagnostic_steps.command: # Talk privately to 3 engineers on adjacent teams. Ask: 'how did you feel about that postmortem?' Look for: 'I'd rather not be the one when something breaks'
diagnostic_steps.expected: if multiple engineers avoid risk-taking → chilling effect confirmed

diagnostic_steps.action: Audit history of action items from past postmortems
diagnostic_steps.command: # Linear/Jira/etc: postmortem AIs from last 6 months
diagnostic_steps.expected: <50% completion rate is a culture signal — postmortems aren't producing real change

fix_steps.action: Loop 1 (today): private 1:1 with the engineer. Own the failure of the process, not their failure
fix_steps.command: # Open with 'how are you doing'; explicitly say 'the postmortem went off the rails — that was a process failure I'm responsible for, and I'm going to fix it'; make their continued employment unambiguous
fix_steps.validation: engineer feels heard; not at flight risk

fix_steps.action: Loop 2 (this week): rewrite the postmortem doc blamelessly
fix_steps.command: # Replace names with roles ('the deploy engineer'); reframe each 'X forgot to' as 'process didn't catch'; list contributing factors not 'the cause'; have a senior leader publicly thank the engineer for their honesty
fix_steps.validation: new doc reads as systems analysis, not court transcript

fix_steps.action: Loop 3 (structural): adopt blameless template + tracked action items
fix_steps.command: # Adopt PagerDuty incident response template OR Google SRE Book Ch 15 example\n# Action items into team backlog with owners + deadlines; report completion at sprint reviews
fix_steps.validation: next postmortem follows new template by default

fix_steps.action: Show the team the recovery story (rebuilds adjacent-team trust)
fix_steps.command: # At all-hands: 'we got this postmortem wrong; here's what we changed and why' — visible signal that contradicts the original public-trial
fix_steps.validation: adjacent engineers notice; willingness to take deploy assignments returns over weeks
